content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm trying to connect an RFID reader to a [product_name] module (read-only). From what I understand, the [product_name] family supports [product_name] protocol in client/server mode via Ethernet, so it should be possible. Does anyone know if there’s an existing or DIY 'Serial to [product_name] Protocol' adapter available? Also, I haven’t been able to find the [product_name] (KNX to Ethernet) communication module for sale. However, there are many RS232/485/422 to TCP/UDP adapters online in the $20 range (examples: HLK-RM04; USR-TCP232-2; USR-TCP232-24). Has anyone managed to send data to [product_name] modules using these or similar devices? My application isn’t critical, so I’m open to less conventional hardware options. I’m familiar with competitor products, which offer add-on modules providing multiple MODBUS interfaces and support for integer I/O. I was hoping the similarly-priced [product_name] lineup would have comparable features. If possible, please share this feedback with the development team. Regards

Communication modules for EIB/KNX or ASi bus were only available for earlier [product_name] modules. The newer series is different in both software and hardware, and currently lacks this type of module.
One option could be to connect an earlier generation [product_name] module with a KNX/EIB interface to a newer [product_name] module.

Hi, I haven’t heard of anyone using an RFID reader with [product_name] modules. As for converters, I’ve been using a USB/Ethernet adapter (ASIX AX88772 USB2.0 to Fast Ethernet Adapter) together with [product_name] configuration software for quite some time. Currently, Modbus TCP/IP or RTU is not supported for these devices, as far as I know. There may be gateways from Modbus to [product_name] protocol (TCP/IP), but this isn’t an area I focus on. Hope this is helpful.

Thank you. It turns out this [product_name] model isn’t suitable for my project and, in my opinion, is a step back compared to the earlier series. I purchased the starter kit with specific modules after being led to believe that a KNX communication module was available. If [company_name] can't deliver, why present the module as a current product? It appears [company_name] is developing product lines with overlapping features but without a comprehensive all-in-one solution. Earlier models = various connectivity but no web/app interface. New models = web/app interfaces but fewer connectivity options (such as the mentioned KNX module). Other [product_name] controllers = have broader functionality at double the cost, including more expensive I/O options, but web or mobile app support is only available with additional customized hardware or software. I initially chose [company_name] hoping to find a unified and cost-effective platform, but I’ll now consider other brands like Mitsubishi, Schneider, Eaton, or OMC that meet my requirements more fully. Regards, [user_name]
Hello [user_name], The [product_name] communication module is now available. [url] Here’s the press release: [url]

Hi [user_name], I’m aware that the [product_name] KNX and other I/O modules will eventually be released, and I’m looking forward to that. Unfortunately, neither the announcements nor the press releases specify a concrete availability date for when end users can purchase the [product_name] module. Based on my experience, press releases are mainly for generating interest and limiting competitors’ market share, but do not necessarily indicate immediate product availability. Regards

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated by the limited connectivity and lack of available modules for certain [product_name] devices, particularly when compared to earlier hardware and competitor brands. Delays in releasing promised modules—such as the KNX/Ethernet communication module—and missing features like Modbus support and serial-to-protocol adapters lead to a sense of decreased flexibility and ambiguity in the product line’s development. There are concerns about misleading information regarding module availability, and users clearly desire a unified, versatile, and up-to-date platform.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] modules to support easy connection of serial devices and MODBUS-type interfaces, similar to older and competitor devices. The user also wants clear, transparent communication about availability of modules and looks for a unified, multi-functional platform from [company_name].
